1.note: The term **Saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

1.q: הֵ֣ן יְשַׁלַּ֣ח אִ֣ישׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּ⁠וֹ֩ וְ⁠הָלְכָ֨ה מֵ⁠אִתּ֜⁠וֹ וְ⁠הָיְתָ֣ה לְ⁠אִישׁ אַחֵ֗ר
1.note: Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that a man divorces his wife and she then becomes the wife of another man. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [Suppose a man sends away his wife and she goes from him and becomes another man’s.]

Yahweh is using **sends away** as a common expression of the culture to mean “divorces.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [If a man dismisses his wife by divorcing her]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man** or a specific **wife**. He means husbands and wives in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [any husband sends away his wife]

Yahweh is using **becomes another man’s** as a common expression of the culture to mean “marries another man.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and becomes the wife of another man]

Yahweh is using the question form to remind the people of Judah that the law does not allow a man to take back a wife whom he has divorced. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [he will certainly not return to her again.]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that such a marriage would defile the whole land. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [That land would surely be greatly polluted!]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **polluted**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [Would that land certainly become very defiled]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if unfaithfulness in marriage were a substance that made the land physically **polluted**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [become greatly guilty]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Judah were **a prostitute** who had given herself to **many lovers**. He means that they have worshiped many other gods instead of him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And you have been unfaithful to me by worshiping many other gods]

The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing the people of Judah as if they were one woman, his unfaithful wife. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is using the question form to express how shocking it is that the people of Judah would expect him to take them back. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [and yet you expect to return to me!]

Jeremiah is using **The declaration of Yahweh** to indicate that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

2.note: Yahweh is using **Lift up your eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “look.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Direct your gaze to the barren heights and see]

The implication is that **the barren heights** were the places where the people of Judah went to worship idols. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the barren heights, your places of idol worship]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that there is no place where the people of Judah have not worshiped other gods. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [There is no place where you have not been ravished!]

The expression **been ravished** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Where have men not ravished you]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Judah were a prostitute who **sat** beside **the roads** waiting for men to pass by. He means that they eagerly looked for every chance to worship other gods. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You eagerly waited for every opportunity to worship them]

The pronoun **them** refers to the men whom the woman was waiting for as they passed by on the roads. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [By the roads you sat waiting for men to pass by]

The point of this comparison is that just as **an Arab in the wilderness** waits beside the road to attack the travelers who pass by, so the people of Judah waited eagerly for every chance to worship other gods. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as eagerly as a desert bandit waiting to ambush travelers]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **prostitution** and **evil**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [by prostituting yourself and by doing what is evil]

3.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [So the rains have been completely withheld]

The expression **have been withheld** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. In this context, Yahweh is the one who withheld the showers. Alternate translation: [So I have withheld the showers]

The term **late rains** describes the rain that fell in the spring, shortly before the grain harvest. If your readers would not be familiar with what the late rains are, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and the spring rains]

Yahweh is using **you have the forehead of a prostitute woman** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you are completely shameless.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [yet you are utterly shameless]

4.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the people of Judah for saying such things to him while they continue to sin. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You have just now called to me]

Here the people of Judah are speaking of Yahweh as if he were their **father**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [My protector and provider]

Here Yahweh says that the people of Judah are speaking of him as if he were the husband whom they had married in their youth, **a close friend of my youth**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You have been my devoted companion since my youth]

4.q: הֲ⁠ל֣וֹא מֵ⁠עַ֔תָּה קראתי לִ֖⁠י אָבִ֑⁠י אַלּ֥וּף נְעֻרַ֖⁠י אָֽתָּה
4.note: Some ancient manuscripts read “you called.” The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts read “I have spoken.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

4.q: הֲ⁠ל֣וֹא מֵ⁠עַ֔תָּה קראתי לִ֖⁠י אָבִ֑⁠י אַלּ֥וּף נְעֻרַ֖⁠י אָֽתָּה
4.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Have you not just now called me your father and the close friend of your youth?]

5.note: The people of Judah are using the question form to express their confidence that Yahweh will not stay angry with them forever. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [He will certainly not keep his anger forever! He will not remain watchful against us to eternity!]

The people of Judah are using **keep** as a common expression of the culture to mean “stay angry.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Will he stay angry forever]

Even though the people of Judah had addressed Yahweh directly, they spoke of him in the third person, as **he**, to show respect. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in a respectful form in the second person. Alternate translation: [Will you keep forever]

Yahweh is using **you have done the evils as you can** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you have done all the evil that you were able to do.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but you have committed every evil deed you were able to commit]

Yahweh is using the adjective **evils** as a noun to mean a certain kind of action. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [but you have done evil things]

6.q: וַ⁠יֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗⁠י בִּ⁠ימֵי֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ הַ⁠מֶּ֔לֶךְ
6.note: Jeremiah is using the word translated as **Then** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Here, **the days** represents the time when Josiah was reigning as king. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the time when Josiah was reigning as king]

Yahweh is using the question form to direct Jeremiah’s attention to what the people of Israel had done. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You have seen what apostate Israel has done!]
The pronoun **She** refers to apostate Israel, whom Yahweh has just mentioned. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Apostate Israel herself has walked]

6.q: כָּל הַ֣ר גָּבֹ֗הַּ וְ⁠אֶל תַּ֛חַת כָּל עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָ֖ן
6.note: Yahweh says **every high hill** and **every leafy tree** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [hill after hill and to underneath one leafy tree after another]

7.q: אַחֲרֵ֨י עֲשׂוֹתָ֧⁠הּ אֶת כָּל אֵ֛לֶּה אֵלַ֥⁠י תָּשׁ֖וּב
7.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that after she did all these things, she would return to me]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [After she has done all these detestable things]

The implication is that Judah saw everything that Israel had done and also saw how Yahweh responded to her. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Then her treacherous sister Judah saw all this that Israel had done and how I responded to her]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the kingdom of Judah were the **sister** of the kingdom of Israel. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the treacherous kingdom of Judah, Israel’s close relation]

8.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Israel had **committed adultery**. He means that they worshiped other gods instead of worshiping him, the one to whom they belonged. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [apostate Israel had been unfaithful to me by worshiping other gods]

8.q: שִׁלַּחְתִּ֕י⁠הָ וָ⁠אֶתֵּ֛ן אֶת סֵ֥פֶר כְּרִיתֻתֶ֖י⁠הָ אֵלֶ֑י⁠הָ
8.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if he were a husband who **had given a scroll of her divorce** to his wife and sent her out of his house. He means that he sent the people of Israel away into exile. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I had sent her people into exile and had formally ended my relationship with her]

Yahweh is using the possessive form **a scroll of her divorce** to describe a scroll that was a written record certifying that he had divorced her. If this would not be clear in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a certificate of her divorce]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [But her sister Judah, acting treacherously, did not fear that I would punish her in the same way]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **fear**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [But her sister Judah, acting treacherously, paid no attention to what happened to Israel]

9.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **prostitution** and **thoughtlessness**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [And she prostituted herself because she thought it was a trivial thing]

Here, **the stone** and **the tree** represent “idols made of stone and wood.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [with stone and wooden idols]

10.note: Yahweh uses the phrase **And even in all of this** here to indicate a contrast between what Judah had seen happen to Israel and the way Judah then acted. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And even though her treacherous sister Judah saw all of this]

Here the **heart** represents where a person’s thoughts and intentions exist. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with all her mind and will]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **deceit**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [but only deceitfully]

11.q: צִדְּקָ֥ה נַפְשָׁ֖⁠הּ מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִ⁠בֹּגֵדָ֖ה יְהוּדָֽה
11.note: Yahweh is using **her spirit** to represent the inner lives of the people of Israel themselves. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [has shown herself to be more righteous than treacherously acting Judah]

12.note: The implication is that **the north** refers to the lands where the people of Israel were living in exile. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [toward the north, where the people of Israel are living in exile]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that apostate Israel should return to Yahweh]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Israel could physically **Return** to him. He means that they should stop worshiping other gods and be faithful to him again. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Be faithful to me again, apostate Israel]

Yahweh is using **I shall not cause my face to fall against you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will not look at you angrily.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I shall not look at you with anger]

Yahweh is using the phrase **I shall not keep forever** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will not stay angry with you forever.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will not hold onto my anger against you forever] or [I will not remain angry with you forever]

13.note: Yahweh is using **know your iniquity** as a common expression of the culture to mean “admit that you have sinned.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [confess your wrongdoing] or [acknowledge that you have done wrong]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Only, know that you have acted wickedly]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh your God**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [that you have transgressed against me, Yahweh your God]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Judah were an unfaithful wife who offered herself to **strangers**. He means that they worshiped the gods of foreign nations. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you have worshiped foreign gods]

Here, **my voice** represents what Yahweh said and “listen” represents obeying. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and what I commanded you, you did not obey] or [and you did not obey what I said]
The word **you** is plural here, although the earlier occurrences of “you” in this verse are singular. Use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
See how you translated “listen” in 3:13. Alternate translation: [you did not pay attention]

14.note: Here the masculine term **sons** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [apostatizing children]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if he were the **husband** of the people of Israel. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for I myself am the one to whom you belong]

The implication is that only a small number of the people of Israel will return. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [just a few of you, one from a city and two from a clan]

15.q: וְ⁠נָתַתִּ֥י לָ⁠כֶ֛ם רֹעִ֖ים כְּ⁠לִבִּ֑⁠י וְ⁠רָע֥וּ אֶתְ⁠כֶ֖ם
15.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the leaders whom he would give to his people were **shepherds** who would care for a flock of sheep. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Then I shall give you leaders after my own will, and they will care for you]

Here the **heart** represents where a person’s desires and intentions exist. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [according to my desires]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **knowledge** and **insight**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [and they will shepherd you wisely, knowing and understanding what is right]

The terms **knowledge** and **insight** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [with true understanding]

16.note: The terms **increase** and **be fruitful** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [you will greatly multiply in number]

The pronoun **they** refers to the people of Israel who will be living in the land at that time. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the people living in the land will no longer say]

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh is important to them]

Yahweh is using the possessive form **The Box of the Covenant of Yahweh** to describe the box that contained the tablets on which the covenant that he made with Israel was written. If this would not be clear in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The Box that contains the tablets on which Yahweh wrote his covenant]

Yahweh is using **it will not come up in heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “no one will think about it.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And no one will think about it]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **miss**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [And they will forget about it]

The expression **another will not be made** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one will make another]

17.q: לִ⁠ירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ כִּסֵּ֣א יְהוָ֔ה וְ⁠נִקְוּ֨וּ אֵלֶ֧י⁠הָ כָֽל הַ⁠גּוֹיִ֛ם
17.note: The pronoun **her** refers to Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Jerusalem, ‘the throne of Yahweh,’ and all the nations will gather to that city]

Here, **the throne of Yahweh** represents the place from which Yahweh rules. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the place from which Yahweh rules]
Here, **the name of Yahweh** represents Yahweh himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to Yahweh himself]

17.q: וְ⁠לֹא יֵלְכ֣וּ ע֔וֹד אַחֲרֵ֕י שְׁרִר֖וּת לִבָּ֥⁠ם הָ⁠רָֽע
17.note: Here Yahweh is using the phrase **walk after** to mean that people would pursue their own stubborn desires, following them as a person follows a leader along a road. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they will no longer live according to the stubborn desires of their evil heart]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **stubbornness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [their evil hearts that are stubborn]

18.q: יֵלְכ֥וּ בֵית יְהוּדָ֖ה עַל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
18.note: Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the house of Judah** figuratively means all the people descended from Judah, and **the house of Israel** figuratively means all the people descended from the patriarch Jacob, who was also known as Israel. Alternate translation: [the people of Judah will walk with the people of Israel]

Even though Yahweh has been speaking about the people of Israel and Judah in the third person, here he addresses them directly in the second person as **your fathers**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could continue to speak about them in the third person here. Alternate translation: [the land that I caused their fathers to inherit]

19.q: אֵ֚יךְ אֲשִׁיתֵ֣⁠ךְ בַּ⁠בָּנִ֔ים וְ⁠אֶתֶּן לָ⁠ךְ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ חֶמְדָּ֔ה נַחֲלַ֥ת צְבִ֖י צִבְא֣וֹת גּוֹיִ֑ם
19.note: Yahweh is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of longing. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [I so much wanted to set you among sons and to give to you a pleasant land, the most beautiful heritage among the nations]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Israel were his own **sons**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I would treat you as my own children]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the land were a **heritage** that a father passes on to his children. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the most beautiful land that I could give to any nation]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And I told you to call me your father]

Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Israel had been walking behind him but might then **turn away** to walk in a different direction from him. He means that they would stop living in the manner in which he wants people to live. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you shall not stop living the way I want you to live]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **turn away**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [you shall continue to follow me]

20.q: אָכֵ֛ן בָּגְדָ֥ה אִשָּׁ֖ה מֵ⁠רֵעָ֑⁠הּ כֵּ֣ן בְּגַדְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֛⁠י
20.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a woman dealing treacherously with her companion** betrays the man to whom she belongs, so the people of Israel have betrayed Yahweh, to whom they belong. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Surely, just as an unfaithful wife betrays the husband to whom she belongs, so you have betrayed me, to whom you belong]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **woman**. He means women in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [like a wife who deals treacherously with her husband]

The implication is that **her companion** is the husband to whom the woman is married. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [with her husband]

21.note: The expression **is heard** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [People hear a voice on the bare heights]

Jeremiah is speaking of how the people of Israel live as if that were **ways** or paths along which they were walking, and he speaks of their sinful conduct as making those paths **crooked**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they have perverted their way of life]

Here Jeremiah is speaking as if the people of Israel had **forgotten** Yahweh. He means that they stopped obeying and worshiping him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they have stopped obeying and worshiping Yahweh their God]

22.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the unfaithfulness of the people of Israel were a sickness that he could **heal**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will put an end to your unfaithfulness]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **apostasies**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [I will heal you from turning away from me]
The words **Behold! We come to you** begin what the people of Israel say in reply to Yahweh. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating that a different speaker is now talking.

The people are using the term **Behold** to focus their listeners’ attention on what they are about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Yes]

23.note: Here, **the hills** and **the mountains** represent “the worship of idols that took place there.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Worthless is the idol worship done on the hills, the noisy rituals performed on the mountains]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [truly Yahweh our God is the one who saves Israel]

24.note: The people of Israel use the word **Yet** here to indicate a contrast between Yahweh, who saves them, and Baal, the shameful god who has consumed everything their fathers worked for since their youth. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [But from our youth, Baal has consumed] or [Because we turned from Yahweh, Baal has consumed]

The people of Israel are speaking of **the shame** as if it were a living thing that could have **consumed** what their ancestors worked to gain. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All our lives, because of the shameful idol, we have lost]

Here, **the shame** represents the god Baal, whose worship brought shame on the people, or the shameful worship of idols in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [that shameful idol]

Here, **the toil of our fathers** represents what our ancestors gained by their hard work. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [what our fathers gained by their hard work]

24.q: אֶת צֹאנָ⁠ם֙ וְ⁠אֶת בְּקָרָ֔⁠ם אֶת בְּנֵי⁠הֶ֖ם וְ⁠אֶת בְּנוֹתֵי⁠הֶֽם
24.note: The pronoun **their** refers to **our fathers**, the ancestors of the people who are speaking. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [our ancestors’ flock and their cattle, our ancestors’ sons and their daughters]

25.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **shame** and **humiliation**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [Let us lie down, feeling ashamed, and let us be completely humiliated]

Here the people of Israel are speaking as if **shame** were a place where they could **lie down**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Let us be utterly ashamed]

Here the people of Israel are speaking as if **our humiliation** were a garment that could **cover** them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and let us be completely humiliated]

25.q: אֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ וַ⁠אֲבוֹתֵ֔י⁠נוּ מִ⁠נְּעוּרֵ֖י⁠נוּ וְ⁠עַד הַ⁠יּ֣וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֑ה
25.note: The people of Israel are leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [We ourselves and our fathers have sinned, from our youth and to this day]
